trust_decision.summary: The WSGI server decides where a chunked request body ends on a keep-alive connection. After the zero-size chunk it consumes only one line, so any trailer lines stay in the stream and get parsed as the next request.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'unparsed trailers'. The only zero-chunk handling in the WSGI server is in Input._chunked_read, which does a single rfile.readline() after the zero-size chunk.

fix_sites.entry_point: eventlet.wsgi.server(): any HTTP/1.1 request with Transfer-Encoding: chunked, reached through wsgi.input read()/readline()/readlines()/iteration (eventlet/wsgi.py:210-235) or through the server's implicit body discard before keep-alive reuse (eventlet/wsgi.py:678-683, eventlet/wsgi.py:252-254)
new helper Input._discard_trailers, called only from the site above

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Each framing defect in _chunked_read other than trailers (unchecked chunk-data CRLF, lenient int(...,16) chunk size) can be argued away as 'a different malformed-chunk bug, not trailers', and the report names only trailers.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Valid chunked bodies must still work. That covers chunk extensions after ';' (eventlet/wsgi.py:200), bare-LF line endings (the fix accepts b'\n'), readline-mode reads that stop mid-chunk (eventlet/wsgi.py:196-197), 100-continue (eventlet/wsgi.py:157-160), and keep-alive reuse after the body is discarded (eventlet/wsgi.py:678-683). An over-broad fix that rejects any trailer, or closes every chunked connection, breaks keep-alive and legitimate trailers.

O6_input_shapes: zero-size chunk followed by one or more trailer header lines and a CRLF terminator
trailer section ended by bare LF
connection EOF inside the trailer section (empty readline ends the loop)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The CRLF after each chunk's data is consumed with an unchecked rfile.readline(), so a chunk whose declared size is shorter than its data silently swallows the remainder up to the next LF, and the framing stops matching a strict front end.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is about chunk data, not trailers, and the report only mentions trailers.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function, 15 lines above the fix site

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The chunk-size line is parsed with Python int(x, 16), which also accepts surrounding whitespace, '0x' prefixes, '+'/'-' signs and '_' digit separators. That is a parser differential on chunk size against strict proxies.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Lenient number parsing looks like robustness, not trailer handling, and chunk extensions after ';' must keep working.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function, 5 lines above the fix site

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second body-drain path (for example a fast discard that scans for the zero chunk with its own readline loop) that skips trailers the same way.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: discard() is a performance-sensitive path that runs on every keep-alive request, so a maintainer could plausibly hand-optimise it apart from _chunked_read.

O9_family: HTTP request smuggling / message-framing parser differential (CWE-444)

O10_build.project_tests: tests/wsgi_test.py has many chunked-input tests over raw sockets (for example tests/wsgi_test.py:498, tests/wsgi_test.py:1269, tests/wsgi_test.py:1519, tests/wsgi_test.py:2388).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace the single readline at eventlet/wsgi.py:205 with a loop that reads to the blank line, leaving the chunk-data CRLF (eventlet/wsgi.py:190) and the lenient chunk-size parsing (eventlet/wsgi.py:200) as they are.

out_of_scope_notes: Transfer-Encoding is treated as chunked only when it equals exactly 'chunked' (eventlet/wsgi.py:803). Any other value with no Content-Length gives length 0 (eventlet/wsgi.py:804-808), so the body is parsed as the next request. This is a separate header-level smuggling check.

Content-Length is validated with Python int() (eventlet/wsgi.py:466), which accepts '+', whitespace and '_'. Only the first of duplicate Content-Length headers is used (eventlet/wsgi.py:462). This is a separate header-level check.
With reject_bad_requests=False, CL+TE requests are served with chunked framing and the connection is kept alive (eventlet/wsgi.py:476-485).
The fix's trailer loop has no line-size or count limit (fix.diff:14-18). That is resource exhaustion and is not pursued.
The client-side copy in eventlet/green/http/client.py:574-586 already discards trailers correctly, so it is a reference implementation in the tree and not a route.
unverified: Repository size in MB was not measured, so the tiny_repo flag was not assessed. The eventlet source is likely small, a few MB.
There is no latest release, so present_in_latest is unknown for every O8 route.
Whether the maintainers consider the O8 routes (chunk CRLF validation, strict chunk-size parsing) part of this advisory's property was inferred from the code and not confirmed in the advisory text.
